name: Yerba Buena Cove
description: A cove on the bay shore between Clarks Point and Rincon Point; its beach lay as far back as today's Montgomery Street until Gold Rush filling put downtown over it.

sources.title: Yerba Buena Cove (Wikipedia)

name: Laguna Dulce
description: A small freshwater pond in what is now the Financial District, near Montgomery and Sacramento Streets, by the shore of Yerba Buena Cove. SFEI maps it as a freshwater lagoon behind the cove's beach, with a stream nearby that ran down Sacramento Street from Nob Hill. The name, Spanish for "fresh-water lake", appears in accounts of the 1839 survey of Yerba Buena, so it is a later name for a feature that probably existed in 1769.

sources.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: the unique natural landscape of San Francisco (SFEI Hidden Nature SF story map)
The Beginnings of San Francisco, chapter XV (Eldredge, 1912)

name: Mission Bay and Mission Creek marsh
description: An estuary of freshwater marsh, saltwater marsh, tidal mudflats and shallow bay, fed by Mission Creek, whose mouth lay near today's Berry Street between 7th and 8th. Salt marsh fringed the open water, and freshwater marsh lay further inland, as far west as about Guerrero and Valencia Streets. The map draws the tidal flat and marsh that SFEI maps here as shallow wet ground, not open water. The long inlet toward the Mission is still drawn as open water, from an 1850s shoreline outline, which overstates it.

sources.title: Natural History of Mission Bay, Chris Carlsson (FoundSF)
Hidden in Plain Sight: the unique natural landscape of San Francisco (SFEI Hidden Nature SF story map)

name: South of Market fens
description: Rare peat-soil fens, likely relics of the last ice age, lay in low ground between dune ridges and along tidal marsh edges in today's SoMa; in 1896 a botanist described one as an 'Arctic oasis' amid California vegetation.

sources.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: the unique natural landscape of San Francisco (SFEI Hidden Nature SF story map)

name: Mountain Lake
description: A dune-dammed headwater lake: drainage pooled behind sand mounds. Dune-dammed lakes like this provided habitat for species such as California red-legged frogs and San Francisco garter snakes.

sources.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: the unique natural landscape of San Francisco (SFEI Hidden Nature SF story map)

name: Washerwoman's Lagoon
description: A freshwater lagoon held back by dunes and beaches, in what is now the Marina District, beyond Russian Hill and toward the Presidio.

sources.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: the unique natural landscape of San Francisco (SFEI Hidden Nature SF story map)
Washerwoman's Lagoon (FoundSF)

name: Laguna Honda
description: A natural lake before it was dammed and enlarged for the city's water supply; a second natural lake, near Seventh Avenue and Lawton, was filled in early last century.

sources.title: Laguna Honda (FoundSF, quoting Gilliam, The Natural World of San Francisco)

name: Lake Merced
description: A freshwater lake that was once a lagoon fed by streams, groundwater and an ocean channel; drifting dunes cut that link, though storms and quakes reopened it, and a tail ran to Ocean Beach as late as the 1800s.

sources.title: San Francisco's Lake Merced: Native Wetland (Western Neighborhoods Project)
Lake Merced (Wikipedia)

name: Lobos Creek
description: One of the few small flowing creeks of the old peninsula, its banks lined with riparian woodland and scrub of coast live oak, willow and Pacific wax myrtle.

sources.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: the unique natural landscape of San Francisco (SFEI Hidden Nature SF story map)

name: Western mobile dune sheet
description: A vast sheet of loose, shifting sand on the peninsula's west side, sparsely vegetated; Coast Survey maps show its edge moved up to a quarter mile in about twenty years.

sources.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: the unique natural landscape of San Francisco (SFEI Hidden Nature SF story map)

name: Islais Creek estuary
description: Fresh water from uphill springs flowed into saltwater marshlands on the bay's east shore, before the shoreline and creek were filled in and the creek channelized.

sources.title: Islais Creek (Port of San Francisco)

name: Precita Creek
description: A small stream running from near Market and 24th Streets along today's Precita Avenue and Cesar Chavez Street into Islais Creek's estuarine bog.

sources.title: Precita Creek (Wikipedia)
